issues.detail: The Greek 'τιμη και δοξα' (honor and glory) is the subject of the verb 'εστιν' (implied/is), but the Vietnamese structure makes 'vinh dự và vinh hiển' (honor and glory) appear as a separate descriptor or part of a different clause construction. More importantly, the Greek says 'honor and glory [are] to the ages of ages', whereas the Vietnamese implies they 'belong to' (thuộc về) the King of ages.
The Greek 'μονω σοφω' (the only wise) is rendered as 'có một và khôn sáng' (has one and wise/bright), which distorts the superlative/unique nature of 'monos' (only/alone).
